nodes.name: Oleylamine reduction synthesis
nodes.procedure: Au₃Ir nanoalloys were prepared using oleylamine as both the reducing and capping agents.
nodes.source_text: Au₃Ir nanoalloys were prepared using oleylamine as both the reducing and capping agents.

nodes.name: Nanoparticle assembly on SHINs
nodes.procedure: A Au core-silicashell-Au₃Ir satellite superstructure was developed by assembling Au₃Ir nanoalloys onto the surface of Au@SiO₂ SHINs. 120-nm Au nanoparticles coated with a 2-nm silica shell were used in these experiments.

nodes.source_text: a Au core-silicashell-Au₃Ir satellite superstructure (inset of Figure 1c) was developed by assembling Au₃Ir nanoalloys onto the surface of Au@SiO₂ SHINs [Note: 120-nm Au nanoparticles coated with a 2-nm silica shell were used in these experiments

properties.description: Bright purple spherical cluster indicating iridium nanoparticles

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in 1.0 M HClO₄ at pH 0
nodes.source_text: The Au₃Ir displays an outstanding overpotential of 246 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... The relative minimum Tafel value (57.8 mV dec⁻¹) further verifies the fastest oxygen evolution kinetics for Au₃Ir.

nodes.description: OER stability testing - ADT and chronopotentiometry in 0.1 M HClO₄
nodes.source_text: after 10000 cycles of accelerated degradation tests (ADTs), it was found that the performance of Au₃Ir remains almost unchanged... the chronopotentials suggest that the overpotential of Au₃Ir at 10 mA cm⁻² remains almost unchanged after 20 h testing.

nodes.description: OER performance comparison across different pH values
nodes.source_text: With the decrease of the pH value, the OER overpotential first decreases then increases, leading to an optimized value at pH = 0 (1.0 M HClO₄).

nodes.description: OER mass activity and TOF at 1.6 V vs RHE in 1.0 M HClO₄
nodes.source_text: Au₃Ir showed the best TOF (3.37 s⁻¹)≈19.8 times larger than the Ir/C (0.17 s⁻¹) and 3.7 times larger than the IrO₂ (0.91 s⁻¹) commercial catalyst. The mass activity of Au₃Ir (6.76 A mg⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows uniform spherical Au₃Ir nanoparticles with average diameter of ≈5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The obtained Au₃Ir nanoalloys show a uniform spherical structure with an average diameter of ≈5 nm (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform distribution of Au₃Ir nanoparticles on the surface of SHINs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM, TEM, and EDX mapping results in Figure 1c clearly show a uniform distribution of Au₃Ir nanoparticles on the surface of the SHINs.

properties.description: Spherical nanoparticles with rough surface morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping demonstrates homogeneous distribution of Au and Ir elements in Au₃Ir nanoalloys.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additional EDX mapping results demonstrate the homogeneous distribution of the Au and Ir elements (Figure S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms atomic ratio of Au to Ir is ≈3:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Combined with the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) results, the atomic ratio of Au to Ir is ≈3:1 (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms alloy structure with crystal plane peaks shifted to higher degree indicating Au lattice shrinkage due to Ir insertion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The alloy structure of the catalyst was further confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD). The crystal plane peaks of Au₃Ir are shifted to a high degree (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows decreased (111) interplanar spacing of 0.21 nm compared to Au (111).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, a decreased (111) interplanar spacing of 0.21 nm compared with Au (111) measured from HR-TEM images further supports the above conclusion (Figure S3, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Au L₃-edge EXAFS shows Au-Au (CN 5.9) and Au-Ir (CN 2.5) bonds; Ir L₃-edge shows Ir-O (CN 1.2), Ir-Ir (CN 2.6), Ir-Au (CN 5.3) bonds confirming nanoalloy structure with partially oxidized Ir.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Only the Au-Au and Au-Ir bonds are visible in the EXAFS spectra of the Au L₃-edge on Au₃Ir, accompanied by coordination numbers (CN) of 5.9 and 2.5, respectively... the FT-EXAFS pattern of the Ir L₃-edge in Au₃Ir suggests the presence of three types of bonds: Ir-O, Ir-Ir, and Ir-Au with CN of 1.2, 2.6, and 5.3, respectively.

properties.description: Iridium with three gold atoms coordination shell
Normalized XAS spectrum showing Au L-edge
Fourier Transform magnitude of Au R-space

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Au 4f shifts to higher binding energy and Ir 4f to lower binding energy compared to pure metals; Ir⁴⁺ species observed confirming partial oxidation of Ir.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Au₄f in Au₃Ir shifts to a higher binging energy while Ir₄f shifts to a lower value compared with pure Au or Ir, respectively... In addition, Ir⁴⁺ species are observed in Au₃Ir further confirming the partial oxidation of Ir.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Ir L₃-edge XANES shows white line enhancement indicating high valence Ir formation during OER; Ir-O coordination number increases from 1.29 to 2.6 (stage 1), more rapidly at OER onset (stage 2), then stabilizes; Ir-O bond length shortens with potential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The white line of Ir L₃-edge XANES spectra is significantly enhanced with the increasing potential indicating the formation of a high valence Ir state during the OER... At stage 1 (1.1 - 1.4 V vs RHE), the coordination number of Ir-O increases continuously from 1.29 to 2.6.

nodes.characterization_summary: SHINERS identifies *OO peroxy intermediate at 821 cm⁻¹ adsorbed on IrOₓ sites during OER; peak intensity correlates with Ir-O coordination number changes; isotopic labeling confirms *OO from water (AEM mechanism).
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the potential reaches 1.55 V, a distinct peak at 821 cm⁻¹ appears... the peak 821 cm⁻¹ can be attributed to the *OO intermediate that appears during the oxygen evolution process.
